Appreciate the clear ask and the questionnaire. High-level answers up-front so you can continue procurement work:

- Classification: For clinical decision support use cases, we treat the combination of model + deployment as a high-risk system under the EU AI Act when decisions materially affect patient care. Hosted API is usable with customer-side controls but we recommend Dedicated or Private for high-risk workloads because of isolation, auditability, and contractual SLAs.

- Controls mapping: we will provide a short mapping doc aligned to NIST AI RMF (Identify/Protect/Detect/Respond/Recover) and reference artifacts (SOC 2, audit logs, KMS integration).

- Evaluation/regression approach: we attach a one-page "redwood-eval-summary.pdf" and a detailed "regression-sampling-plan.xlsx". In brief: periodic automated regression runs (weekly for high-risk prompts), stratified sampling across prompt clusters, behavioral checks (accuracy, hallucination, safety signals), drift thresholds defined per signal with automated alerts + canary rollouts + automatic fallback to a safety model.

- Evidence bundle: see attachments (we can produce a tailored packet for your procurement folder).

Team —

Following Sean's reply to Aegis, here's a proposed breakdown for the RFP evidence and the short mapping doc. I attached draft_responses.docx to this thread (internal). Key points:

1) EU AI Act classification + recommended contractual approach
   - Position: model+use-case determines classification. For CDS (clinical decision support) we recommend "high-risk" classification. For procurement: include a deployment addendum that mandates Dedicated/Private with defined audit retention and explicit rollback SLAs.

2) NIST AI RMF mapping (one page):
   - Identify: asset inventory (models, datasets), model card + versioning
   - Protect: KMS/HSM keys, access controls, tenancy isolation, runtime auth
   - Detect: latency/anomaly metrics, model output monitoring (safety filters), drift scoring
   - Respond: automated canary rollback, human-in-the-loop alert workflows, incident postmortem template
   - Recover: snapshot-based rollback, archived evaluation snapshots, continuity runbooks

3) Regression/eval sampling plan (detailed in regression-sampling-plan.xlsx):
   - Sampling: stratified by prompt intent, severity index, and token-length distribution; minimum weekly sample of 1,000 prompts for high-risk buckets, monthly for lower-risk
   - Drift thresholds: F1/precision/recall thresholds per task + hallucination rate limit (e.g., <1% for critical templates). Alerts at 3-sigma sustained or 5% absolute increase vs baseline
   - Playbook: automated flag -> cohort replay -> canary against gold-labeled prompts -> rollback threshold -> customer notification + remediation plan
   - Example test case: clinical-discharge-summary prompt set (200 prompts): expected entity extraction accuracy > 94%, hallucination rate < 1%.

4) Artifacts to attach to procurement packet:
   - redwood-eval-summary.pdf (executive summary of our eval approach)
   - regression-sampling-plan.xlsx (detailed sampling + thresholds)
   - SOC2-excerpt.pdf (SOC 2 Type II scope page) — request from security to produce a short excerpt for procurement
   - Model-card-example.json (anonymized) — internal reference

Next steps: Aditya + Karthik to finalize the NIST mapping and produce the one-pager. Marissa to coordinate SOC2 excerpt request and confirm retention SLA language. Sean to confirm call time with Aegis.

Neha
